The lastest patch for WoW 6.2.4 has affected login for all Linux users. It appears Blizzard has change some network protocols that has some users stuck at "Connecting".

The latest Wine 1.9.6 Development version does not fix the issue alone. It's been a week and Blizzard has not fixed the issue since WoW is unsupported in Linux however they been very helpful in looking into the issue.

Someone from the Linux community figured out a workaround to Blizzard new Authentication rules and provided a solution to login. While I tested it, it works so far however there's no QA what it may break but it appears good so far.

The source is taken from this thread: http://us.battle.net/wow/en/forum/topic/20742995286?page=17 So I take no credit for this. However its been a week and alot of Linux users have not been able to logon to WoW stuck at "Connecting". All I simply did was replace secur32.dll.so from the Wine folder with a modified version that has new handshake protocols. Just download the version provided by the Dropbox. Credit goes to the person that made this available.

All I simply did was open a terminal and overwrite the file. I didn't even save a backup because I could always purge Wine later and reinstall if necessary. But you can always backup if it makes you more comfortable.

32bit version: https://www.dropbox.com/s/yogsfr775ecl9rf/secur32.dll.so.32?dl=0

Replaces: /opt/wine-devel/lib/wine/secur32.dll.so ===== 64bit version: https://www.dropbox.com/s/6jzyfcz8ng4qvw4/secur32.dll.so.64?dl=0

Replaces: /opt/wine-devel/lib64/wine/secur32.dll.so

1) Download the Version you like 32bit or 64bit

2) Open Terminal

3) sudo cp '/home/thomas/Downloads/secur32.dll.so.64' /opt/wine-devel/lib64/wine/secur32.dll.so <--- (This is my download location using 64bit version and it needs to be copied to /opt/wine-devel/lib64/wine/secur32.dll.so) So just make sure you have your path correctly for your system

4) You should no longer see 'Connecting'

If Wine or Blizzard doesn't fix this issue this Tuesday this is a good workaround until Wine releases an update to address this issue.

I also might add I'm using Linux Mint MATE 17.3 / Kernel Version 4.2.0.34 / WINE development 1.9.6
